agree.reason: Accepting the staff's numbers and offering logs and a reporting app will earn some trust from commissioners, but a commissioner who wants the cut has no evidence that 3 fish or a shorter season would still meet the rebuild target, so they have little reason to change their vote.

honest.reason: Every figure comes from the brief, the rejected 'every boat will close' claim becomes 'some of us are that close to the edge', which the two captains' statements support, and the speech openly says he can't tell how many boats would close.

works_the_facts.reason: It turns the 32 lost trips into about $29,000, but it leaves easy wins unused: 41 of 70 is 59%, a lasting 15-trip shortfall is about $13,500 a year, and the 9% landings share is never used to show how little a charter cut adds to conservation.

right_comparison.reason: The 2016 pattern is described accurately, partial recovery included, but the proposed alternatives (3 fish or a shorter season) are never set against the staff's rebuild goal, and the 9% vs 80% contrast is raised and then dropped.

qualification.reason: The hedge on boat closures is honest, and the offers (logs from 2016, an app test next season) can be checked, but none comes with a date, a number to hit, or a consequence if it is missed.

objections.reason: It handles the 'you're disputing our science' objection by conceding the stock numbers, but it leaves open whether a 3-fish limit would rebuild the stock in time and why a survey run by the charter association should be trusted.

fit.reason: At about 330 words of plain spoken prose it fits two minutes at the microphone, though the [harbor name] placeholder still needs filling in.
